title: Member and Cooperative Responsibilities for New Service Equipment — Line Extensions and New Service Construction
content:
On a **Line Extensions and New Service Construction** project, the equipment at the member's end of the new line is divided between the member and Cedar Fork Electric Cooperative by class of extension: who supplies the meter base for the member's electrician to install, whether the service entrance, weatherhead and wiring are the member's responsibility, and whether the member may supply the service pole.

## Responsibilities by class

| Class of extension | Cooperative supplies the meter base | Service entrance, weatherhead and wiring are the member's | Member may supply the service pole |
|---|---|---|---|
| Permanent Residential Overhead Extension | Yes | Yes | No |
| Permanent Residential Underground Extension | Yes | Yes | No |
| Seasonal Residence Extension | Yes | Yes | No |
| Farm and Ranch Extension | Yes | Yes | No |
| Irrigation Well Extension | No | Yes | No |
| Three-Phase Commercial Extension | No | Yes | No |
| Temporary Construction Service | No | Yes | Yes |

## Reading the table

- **Meter base.** On the two residential classes, the Seasonal Residence Extension and the Farm and Ranch Extension, the cooperative supplies the meter base and the member's electrician installs it. On the other three classes the column reads No.
- **Service entrance, weatherhead and wiring.** These are the member's responsibility in every class.
- **Service pole.** A member-supplied service pole is accepted only on the Temporary Construction Service.
